title: Formation of the ozone layer
summary: Blue-green algae began releasing oxygen through photosynthesis long before an ozone layer could form. By about 600 million years ago, when oxygen stood at about 10% of today's level, enough ozone is believed to have existed to shield Earth from lethal ultraviolet light of 200 to 300 nanometres. Until then, life was restricted to the ocean. The ozone layer enabled organisms to develop and live on land.

as_recorded.value: The amount of ozone required to shield Earth from biologically lethal UV radiation, wavelengths from 200 to 300 nanometers (nm), is believed to have been in existence 600 million years ago.
Around 600 million years ago, a thin ozone layer formed that was capable of protecting life from harmful wavelengths of UV radiation

where.modern_name: Worldwide; stand-in pin at the Rhynie Chert, Scotland

paleo.not_applicable: Global atmospheric process; geometry is global.

importance.justification: The ozone layer made life on land possible.

related.because: Photosynthetic cyanobacteria generated the atmospheric molecular oxygen required to form ozone in the stratosphere.
Attenuation of surface ultraviolet radiation allowed multicellular organisms to diversify into shallow marine environments.
